bc_solar_caves.blurb: A small cluster of cave boulders in the Silver Lake area of the Fraser Valley, around 290 m above sea level. Seven problems are on record, spanning moderate lines up to a few very hard ones near the top of the V scale, so the place leans toward strong boulderers. The caves sit in a dip among thick shrubs, a roughly 500 m stream-side walk beyond the first boulder you reach. They fill with water through the wet months, which leaves every problem caked in mud until they dry out.

bc_roche_lake_boulders.blurb: Three boulders tucked below the Roche Lake sport crag, roughly forty minutes outside Kamloops at about 1,140 m elevation. Seven problems run from easy to one very hard line, with most in the V0 to V4 range, which makes the spot useful for newer boulderers and as a warm-up before the roped routes. Landings are uneven and rocky, so bring spotters for the harder problems. The dirt road in is long and parking is tight, so sharing a vehicle helps.

bc_mount_robson.blurb: The highest summit in the Canadian Rockies, at 3,954 m inside Mount Robson Provincial Park. Its north side is heavily glaciated, with a long ice face dropping toward the Berg Glacier, while the south side is a tangle of rock and snow ridges. Seven routes are on record: mostly moderate ice and snow lines around WI3, one at WI4, and one alpine rock route with fifth-class climbing. Weather often forces parties back, and only a small share of attempts reach the top.

bc_yoho_valley_road_ice.blurb: Waterfall ice lining the Yoho Valley Road, near Field in Yoho National Park, one of the densest collections of ice climbs in the Canadian Rockies. Seven climbs are on record, from WI3 up to WI6, with the bulk in the WI4 to WI5 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on steep ice. Most routes require crossing the Yoho River, which is only safe once it is well frozen. Approach slopes can be exposed to avalanche, and many lines form fairly early in the season.
